extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners/agents, and USPTO staff involved in filing or processing PCT (international) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for filing and processing PCT (international) applications at the United States Receiving Office, including applicant eligibility, representation/powers of attorney, forwarding to the International Bureau, access to electronic filing, and the conditions for an international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence of the Receiving Office and forwarding under PCT Rule 19.4
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT Rule 19.4 provides for transmittal of an international application to the International Bureau as Receiving Office in certain instances (e.g., when the international application is filed with the United States Receiving Office and the language in which the international application is filed is not accepted by the United States Receiving Office, or if the applicant does not have the requisite residence or nationality). The Receiving Office of the International Bureau will consider the international application to be received as of the date accorded by the United States Receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forwarding avoids loss of filing date when the U.S. RO is not competent but the application indicates an applicant to be a national or resident of a PCT Contracting State or is in a language accepted by the IB. Where no residence or nationality is indicated, the U.S. is not competent and the application will be forwarded to the IB as RO provided the necessary fee (equal to the transmittal fee) is paid. If all applicants are residents/nationals of non-PCT Contracting States, Rule 19.4 does not apply and the application is denied an international filing date. Transfer requests may be declined if received after substantial processing by the U.S. RO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-of-receipt vs. date-of-deposit warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Although U.S. law authorizes rules that consider a paper filed on the date deposited with USPS, PCT Rule 20.1(a) provides for marking the 'date of actual receipt on the request.' Applicants should be aware of possible different interpretations by foreign authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious using Priority Mail Express® or similar practices; different authorities may interpret the filing/receipt date differently. Check MPEP § 1834.01 and consult the PCT Help Desk or U.S. Receiving Office for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing license requirement for IB-filed or forwarded international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application filed with, or forwarded to, the International Bureau must have a foreign filing license unless: (1) the invention was not made in the United States; or (2) a U.S. national application on the invention was filed at least six months prior to the filing of the international application, the U.S. national application is not subject to a secrecy order under 37 CFR 5.2, and the application does not contain amendments or modifications changing the general nature of the invention in a manner that would require corresponding U.S. application inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 5.11 and 5.15 for details. Ensure compliance with foreign filing license rules before filing or forwarding to the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility and nationality/residence requirements (PCT Art. 9, Rule 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any resident or national of a Contracting State may file an international application. The applicant can be an individual, corporate entity or other concern. Where there are two or more applicants, at least one of them must be a national or a resident of a Contracting State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an applicant is a resident or national depends on the national law of that State and is decided by the Receiving Office. Possession of a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in a Contracting State may be considered residence; a legal entity constituted under a Contracting State's law is considered a national.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of inventor when inventor is not the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventor is not the applicant, indications concerning the inventor must nevertheless be made in the Request where the national law of at least one of the designated States requires that the name of the inventor be furnished at the time of filing a national application (PCT Rule 4.1(a)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'inventor only' check-box, indicate inventor’s name and address in Box III, and omit inventor’s residence and nationality when required. Consult PCT Applicant’s Guide Annexes B1/B2 for States that require such indications. Most national phases require inventor information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file in the U.S. Receiving Office (37 CFR 1.421 post-AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only residents or nationals of the United States of America may file international applications in the United States Receiving Office. If an international application does not include an applicant indicated as a U.S. resident or national and at least one applicant (1) has indicated a residence or nationality in a PCT Contracting State, or (2) has no residence or nationality indicated, applicant will be notified and, if the international application includes an equivalent fee, the application will be forwarded to the International Bureau acting as Receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For designation of the United States at national stage, the international application will be accepted by the USPTO for the national stage only if the applicant is the inventor or other person as provided in §§ 1.422 or 1.424. Registered attorneys or agents may sign and file, but separate powers of attorney may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for applicant where inventor is deceased or incapacitated (37 CFR 1.422 / pre-AIA provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is deceased or under legal incapacity, the legal representative of the inventor may be an applicant in an international application which designates the United States. For international applications having filing dates before Sept 16, 2012, only inventors (and legal representatives of deceased or legally incapacitated inventors) could be applicants for purposes of the U.S. designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indicating a legal representative in the Request, follow the specified format (e.g., 'SMITH, Alfred, legal representative of JONES, Bernard (deceased)') and indicate whether the legal representative is 'applicant only' or 'applicant and inventor' as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of agent, attorney, or common representative (PCT Rule 90 / 37 CFR 1.455)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment must be effected either in the Request form (signed by applicant), in the Demand form, or in a separate power of attorney submitted either to the U.S. Receiving Office or to the International Bureau. If applicants have not appointed an attorney/agent or one applicant to represent them, and there is more than one applicant, the applicant first named in the request who is entitled to file in the U.S. RO shall be considered the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney or agent may appoint an associate who then is of record (PCT Rule 90.1(d)). Appointment revokes any earlier appointment unless otherwise indicated (PCT Rule 90.6(b),(c)). Powers of attorney and revocations should be submitted to the U.S. RO until issuance of the international search report. The addressee for correspondence is indicated in section 108 of the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and formalities for submitting a separate power of attorney (PCT Rule 90.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate power of attorney shall be submitted to either the Receiving Office or the International Bureau, subject to Rule 90.5 and 90.4(b)-(c). If the separate power of attorney is not signed, or if required information does not comply with Rule 4.4, it is considered nonexistent unless corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a POA appoints an agent to represent before an ISA or IPEA, it must be submitted to that Authority. Receiving Offices and Authorities may waive the requirement for submission in many cases, but the waiver does not apply to certain withdrawals (Rules 90 bis). The Customer Number Practice may not be used to appoint an agent in the international phase; a POA using customer number will be considered nonexistent unless corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: General power of attorney (PCT Rule 90.5) — deposit and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'general' power of attorney (appointing an agent to represent the applicant in any international application) may be referred to in the request or demand provided the general POA has been deposited and a copy is attached to the request/demand. The general POA must be deposited with the Receiving Office or, where appropriate, with the ISA/IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy attached need not be signed. Offices/Authorities may waive the requirement for the attached copy in some cases, but a copy must be submitted when an agent files certain withdrawal notices. General POAs are recognized for filing and prosecuting international applications and become effective for particular applications when properly referred to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of requirement for a separate power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT Rules 90.4(d) and 90.5(c) allow the Receiving Office, International Bureau, ISAs and IPEAs to waive the requirement for a separate POA or copy of a general POA in all cases except notices withdrawing international applications, designations, priority claims, demands or elections (PCT Rule 90 bis). The USPTO, when acting as RO/ISA/IPEA, will in most cases waive the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate POA or copy may still be required where an agent’s authority is in doubt or waiver could harm an applicant (e.g., removal of an applicant). Model POA forms are available from WIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation and renunciation of appointment of agent/common representative (PCT Rule 90.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appointment of an agent or common representative may be revoked by the persons who made the appointment or their successors in title; any appointment of a sub-agent by that agent is also considered revoked. An agent or common representative may renounce his appointment by a notification signed by him. Appointment of a new agent or common representative will, unless otherwise indicated, revoke earlier appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 90.4(b) and (c) apply, mutatis mutandis, to documents containing revocations/renunciations. If appointment was effected by a separate POA, that POA must be submitted to the Receiving Office or IB. Customer Number Practice cannot be used to revoke by reference to customer number in international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of practitioner and USPTO requirements (procedural and ethical duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. attorneys or agents wishing to withdraw from representation in international applications may request to do so; the request should indicate mailing addresses. The Office will not accept address changes to a new practitioner absent filing of a power of attorney to the new representative. Because the USPTO does not recognize law firms, each attorney of record must sign the withdrawal notice or there must be clear indication of one attorney signing on behalf of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 11.116, USPTO usually requires practitioner(s) to certify they gave reasonable notice to the client prior to the reply period expiring and delivered to the client all papers and property. Withdrawal requests that do not conform to 37 CFR 11.116 may be denied. The Office will not approve withdrawal requests where the practitioner was not appointed in a POA but is acting under 37 CFR 1.34; practitioner remains responsible for correspondence filed while acting in representative capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Customer Number Practice in the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The Customer Number Practice set forth in MPEP § 403 may not be used in the international phase to appoint an agent or designate a correspondence address. A POA using the Customer Number Practice will be considered nonexistent unless corrected. A Customer Number may be used in the international phase solely for viewing the international application in the USPTO electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish or change correspondence address or to appoint or change an agent in the international phase, follow PCT Rule 92 bis procedures (written request to U.S. RO or IB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to USPTO patent electronic filing system and associating customer numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information is available via the USPTO patent electronic filing system with public and private views. Private view requires registered Patent Center users and allows access to non-public application information for associated applications. To associate a new international application filed via USPTO system with an existing customer number, enter the customer number when filling in the application data; to associate a previously filed international application, submit Form PTO-2248 with required information and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associating a customer number permits viewing but does not allow establishing/changing correspondence address or appointing/changing an agent. The IB will not record a change in agent if the change is received after the expiration of 30 months from the priority date (see PCT Rule 92 bis). Changes must be made under PCT Rule 92 bis through a written request to the U.S. RO or IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for an international filing date (PCT Article 11 / 37 CFR 1.431)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall contain a Request, a description, one or more claims, an abstract, and one or more drawings (where required). The Receiving Office shall accord an international filing date provided that at the time of receipt: (i) at least one applicant is a United States resident or national (for U.S. RO), (ii) the application is in the prescribed language (English), and (iii) the application contains at least: an indication that it is an international application, designation of at least one Contracting State, the name of the applicant, a part which on its face appears to be a description, and a part which on its face appears to be a claim or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of international filing, transmittal, and search fees may be made in full at filing or within one month; if fees are not paid within one month and prior to notice of deficiency, applicant will be given a one-month non-extendable time to pay deficient fees plus a late payment fee. If required payments to cover fees and late payment fee are not timely made, the Receiving Office will declare the international application withdrawn under PCT Article 14(3)(a). The international filing date is the earliest date on which the PCT Article 11(1) requirements were satisfied; if not satisfied at initial receipt, the RO will invite the applicant to correct defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of an international application designating the United States (35 U.S.C. 363)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application designating the United States shall have the effect, from its international filing date under Article 11 of the Treaty, of a national application for patent regularly filed in the Patent and Trademark Office (subject to pre-AIA exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications subject to pre-AIA rules, see pre-AIA wording in 35 U.S.C. 363 and Appendix R. Ensure compliance with national stage entry requirements.
